transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my eating has been really off for months. Some days I barely pick at toast and coffee, and then other days I’m in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy. It’s just gotten all turned around.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past few months?
I don’t know if it’s been a big weight loss exactly. My eating has just been really uneven for months—some days it’s just toast and coffee, and other days I’m buying sweets I don’t even really want.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
No, not really. I don’t think it’s about being afraid of gaining weight. My eating just feels kind of all over the place.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you couldn't stop?

Not exactly like I couldn’t stop. It’s more that my eating has been all turned around for months—some days I just pick at toast and coffee, and other days I’m in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.
Do you usually feel guilty after eating?
Not usually, no. I might feel kind of disappointed in myself if I’ve been eating junk, but I wouldn’t say I usually feel guilty after eating.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating on the days you buy a lot of sweets?

I wouldn’t say I feel totally out of control, no. It’s more like my eating is just turned around lately. Some days I barely want anything, like toast and coffee, and then other days I end up standing there buying a bunch of sweets I don’t even really want.
Do you notice that your eating changes in response to how you're feeling?

Yes, I think so. When I’m feeling worse, my eating gets really off. Some days I just pick at toast and coffee, and then other days I end up in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even enjoy much. It’s been like that for months.
Do you think your mood influences what you eat on a given day?

Yes, I do think it does. When my mood is worse, my eating gets really turned around. Some days I’m just picking at toast and coffee, and other days I’m in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy. It’s been going on for months now.
Are you eating sweets or other foods in an attempt to improve your mood on the days you're feeling worse?

I don’t really think it’s to improve my mood, exactly. It’s more that my eating has been all turned around for months. Some days I’m barely picking at toast and coffee, and other days I end up standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.
Do you think eating sweets or other foods helps you feel better when you're feeling down?

Not really. I mean, I buy the sweets sometimes, but I don’t feel better after. My eating has just been all over the place for months—some days it’s just toast and coffee, and other days I’m in the bakery aisle getting things I don’t even really enjoy.
Are you using food as a way to deal with your emotions when you're feeling down?

I don’t think I’m doing it on purpose to deal with feelings, no. It’s more that my eating has been messed up for months. Some days I just pick at toast and coffee, and other days I end up buying sweets in the bakery aisle that I don’t even really want.
Do you often find yourself not being interested in food when you're not eating much?

Yes, on those days I’m not really interested in food. I’ll just pick at something like toast and coffee and not want much else. It’s been like that for months, sort of back and forth with the days where I end up buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.
Do you feel like you've lost your appetite on the days you're barely eating?

Yes, on those days it does feel like I’ve lost my appetite. I’ll just have toast and coffee and kind of pick at it. It’s been going on for months, back and forth with the days where I end up buying sweets I don’t really enjoy.
Do you think your lack of interest in food on some days is related to your emotional state or is it just a physical feeling of not being hungry?

I think it’s tied up with how I’m feeling, at least some. My eating has been all turned around for months now—some days I can barely pick at toast and coffee, and then other days I’m standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.
Is your lack of appetite on certain days more because you're not feeling hungry physically or because you're just not interested in eating due to how you're feeling emotionally?

It feels more connected to how I’m feeling than just being physically hungry or not. My eating’s been all turned around for months—some days I just pick at toast and coffee, and other days I’m buying sweets in the bakery aisle that I don’t even really enjoy.
Do you feel hungry at all on the days you're barely eating?

Not really, no. On those days I’m not thinking much about food—I’ll just pick at toast and coffee. It’s been like that for months, kind of back and forth with the days I end up buying sweets I don’t even enjoy.
Do you think there's a specific feeling or emotion that triggers your desire to eat sweets on some days?

I don’t know if it’s one specific feeling. It’s more that my eating has just been all turned around for months. Some days I barely have toast and coffee, and then other days I find myself in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.
On the days you're barely eating, is it because you're not interested in food or because you're trying not to eat?

It’s more that I’m just not interested in food. I’m not trying not to eat. My eating’s just been all turned around for months—some days I only pick at toast and coffee, and other days I’m buying sweets I don’t even really want.
Are you intentionally restricting your food intake on the days you're barely eating?

No, I’m not doing it on purpose. It’s just… my eating’s been all turned around for months. Some days I only pick at toast and coffee, and other days I’m standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.
Do you think your eating pattern of having some days with very little food and other days with a lot of sweets is related to feeling sad or depressed?

Yes… I think it probably is. Most days I wake up with this heavy sadness on me, like it’s already there before anything happens. Even when I’m in the kitchen with the coffee going, everything just feels kind of cold or empty. So I think the eating gets mixed up with that.
